ai.description: This toad reaches 40–50 mm. It is brown with dark dorsal markings and a pale belly. Distinctive features include a prominent, convex vent and a sharp, fleshy projection on the upper eyelid.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys pachyproctus* is best distinguished by the prominent, fleshy, rounded projection located on the vent, which is absent in other Indian *Megophrys* species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys pachyproctus* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and montane streams in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Megophrys pachyproctus* is a nocturnal predator that remains motionless on the forest floor, relying on its leaf-like camouflage to ambush passing insect prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys pachyproctus* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August). Females lay small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys pachyproctus* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, at elevations between 1,000–2,000m.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Megophrys pachyproctus* consists of a single, short, low-pitched "cluck" or "tok" sound, typically emitted from near streams in montane forests.
